source: CARDI Farmer Notes variety leaflets (KA15, Phka Romdoul, KA4, KA14, IR66, Sen Kraob 01); Climate Resilient Broadcasting Rice Growing Technique, ASPIRE/IFAD, MAFF, 2018
text:
Sun-drying is the standard smallholder method: spread threshed paddy in a thin layer (about 2-3cm thick) on a clean mat, tarpaulin, rubber sheet, or concrete floor -- never directly on bare or contaminated soil -- and turn it periodically. Drying time depends on the weather: full sun needs only about 1 day, turning roughly every half hour; partly cloudy weather needs about 2 days, turning about once an hour; overcast weather with little sun can take up to 3 days, turning about every 2 hours. The target is around 14% moisture content for safe storage, which farmers can approximate using the field ripeness signs (80-85% of grains husk-golden, panicle neck brown, grain hard rather than milky) as a rough proxy when a moisture meter isn't available.

After drying, keep seed paddy completely separate from paddy intended for eating or selling: tie seed paddy tightly in a plastic-lined bag, place that inside an outer sack, and label it clearly with the variety name and harvest date. Store both seed and consumption paddy in a dry, well-ventilated space, off the ground, and protected from rain, rodents, birds, and insects -- a damp or poorly ventilated granary undoes the benefit of careful drying within weeks.
